Comments on a note now work, committed as `472bbf4` on the current branch (not pushed). The gate passes on all steps, including the unit and end-to-end tests. The storm owes nothing and is marked `done: true`.

**How it's built.** Everything stays inside the Notes context, so there was no new context, relationship or ADR.
- **Comment:** a thing of its own that points to its note by id, as the storm decided. Its text is trimmed, required, and at most 500 characters.
- **Who may comment:** a domain service, `NoteCommenting`, checks the note. Only its owner and the accounts it is shared with can comment. Anyone else is told the note doesn't exist, the same answer Notes gives everywhere. An archived note refuses new comments.
- **`POST /notes/{id}/comments`:** answers 202, and the operation's `result` is the new comment's id. An anonymous caller gets 403 straight away.
- **`GET /notes/{id}/comments`:** answers `[{ id, authorId, text, createdAt }]`, oldest first. It gives 404 to anyone who can't read the note and 403 to an anonymous caller. Comments on an archived note stay readable.
- **Tests:** specs cover the comment, the permission check, the command and the query, and the end-to-end suite covers the whole flow.

**One deviation from the usual pattern.** The comment's factory is `Comment.register()`, not `create()`. With two `create()` methods in Notes, the inventory tool decided that "create a note" also produced `NoteCommented`, and the conventions check failed. The tool matches any `<anything>.create(` call against every aggregate's `create`. The contract allows `register()` as the other name, so I used it. The tool itself should probably be fixed so it checks which class a `create(` is called on.

**What was unclear, and what I decided:**
- **Whitespace:** a comment is trimmed before the length check, so a blank comment is refused. This matches how note titles work.
- **Shared then unshared:** if an account is removed from a note's sharing later, it can no longer read or write comments there, and its old comments remain on the note.
- **Same-millisecond comments:** two comments written in the same millisecond are listed in the order they were saved.
- **Archiving race:** a comment sent at the moment the note is being archived can still get through. The archived check reads the note but doesn't lock it. A real store would need a version check on the note to close this, which seemed more than the feature needs.

A note's history now works, committed as `b7278a8` on the current branch (not pushed). The gate passes on every step, including the unit and end-to-end tests. The storm owes nothing and is marked `done: true`.

**How it's built.** Everything stays inside Notes, with no new context, relationship or ADR.
- **Edits keep history:** each edit stores the title and text it replaces as the next numbered version, with the time it was replaced. Version 1 is the note as first written. The current content is not listed as a version.
- **Restoring:** `restoreVersion` follows the storm's decision that restoring is an edit. It records `NoteEdited`, keeps what it replaces as a new version, and is refused on an archived note. It is also refused for a version the note doesn't have. Anyone but the owner gets the usual Notes refusals.
- **`GET /notes/{id}/versions`:** answers `[{ version, title, text, replacedAt }]`, most recent first, to the owner only. It gives 404 to anyone else or for an unknown note, and 403 to an anonymous caller. I kept this list out of `GET /notes/{id}` so that response's shape doesn't change.
- **`POST /notes/{id}/versions/{version}/restore`:** answers 202. A version that doesn't exist, including one that isn't a number, gives an `ERROR` outcome.
- **Tests:** domain specs cover the history, restoring and the refusals; there is a query spec and an end-to-end suite.

**What was unclear, and what I decided:**
- **Where versions live:** inside the Note itself, because the storm names Note as what the restore command acts on and lists no separate fact. History therefore grows with every edit; if notes get edited heavily, it may need to move into its own store later.
- **Unchanged edits:** an edit that changes nothing still creates a version, since the brief says "every time a note's title or text is edited".
- **A version that isn't a number** (`/versions/latest/restore`) gets 202 then an `ERROR` outcome rather than an immediate 400, to match the API table's "an `ERROR` outcome when the version does not exist".
- **Corrupted history:** loading a stored note now throws if one of its saved version titles is invalid, like the rest of the stored note.
- **Unrelated cleanup:** I removed a duplicated doc-comment line in `NoteExceptions.ts`.

Editors now work, committed as `bda8e8b` on the current branch (not pushed). The gate passes on every step, including the unit and end-to-end tests. The storm owes nothing and is marked `done: true`.

**How it's built.** Everything stays inside Notes, with no new context, relationship or ADR.
- **Sharing with a role:** sharing takes a role, `reader` (the default) or `editor`. Sharing again with a different role changes it and records `NoteShared` with the new role, as the storm decided. Readers become editors and back the same way.
- **What an editor can do:** edit the title and text, list and restore versions, and comment. Comments already worked, because an editor is in `sharedWith`. Archiving, restoring the note, pinning, tagging, sharing and reminders stay the owner's.
- **What a reader is told:** a reader who tries to write gets a new refusal, `NotNoteEditor`. Before, they were told `NotNoteOwner`.
- **API answers:**
  - `GET /notes/{id}`: the owner's answer now includes `editors`; editors also stay in `sharedWith`. Editors and readers don't see either list.
  - `GET /notes/{id}/versions`: open to the owner and editors. Each version now has `editedBy`, the account whose edit replaced it.

**What was unclear, and what I decided:**
- **Same role again:** sharing again with the role the account already has is still refused (`NoteAlreadyShared`), the same as sharing twice was before. The brief only said sharing again changes the role.
- **Invalid role:** a role other than `reader` or `editor` gets 202, then an `ERROR` outcome rather than an immediate 400, following how the earlier routes leave validation to the domain.
- **Readers and the history:** a reader still gets 404 on `GET /versions`. The brief allows the list to the owner and editors only.
- **Order of `editors`:** listed in the order accounts became editors.
- **Older events:** `NoteShared` now always carries `role`. Nothing outside Notes subscribes to it today.
- **Corrupted snapshots:** loading a stored note throws if it lists an editor the note isn't shared with.

Deleting an account now works, committed as `5063506` on the current branch (not pushed). The gate passes on every step, including the unit and end-to-end tests. The storm owes nothing and is marked `done: true`.

**Architecture.** This needed new relationships between contexts, so I declared them and wrote a decision record:
- **Context map:** three new links from Accounts, to Notes, Notifications and Plans, each carried by one integration event, `AccountDeleted`. Accounts → Notes already existed through Notes' `AccountDirectory` port; this adds the same pair through the other mechanism.
- **ADR:** `docs/adr/0006-a-deleted-account-is-forgotten-by-every-context.md`, also linked from the ADR index.

**The feature:**
- **`DELETE /accounts/me`:** answers 202, or 403 for an anonymous caller. The account records `AccountDeleted` and is removed from the store. That alone makes its old token anonymous (the authentication already checked that the account exists), makes login with its email 401, and frees the email to sign up again under a new id.
- **Notes:** in its own reaction, it removes the account's notes with everything on them, and its comments on other people's notes. It also removes the account from `sharedWith` and `editors` on the notes shared with it.
- **Notifications:** removes all of the account's notifications, including planned reminders.
- **Plans:** removes the account's plan, if it ever switched.
- **Recorded events:** none of the three reactions records a fact of its own, as the storm requires. Each runs in one transaction, so it all happens or none of it does.
- **Tests:** unit specs cover the account, the command and each of the three reactions. An end-to-end scenario covers the 403 cases, the token, removed notes and comments, the cleared shares, the 401 at login, and signing up again.

**What was unclear, and what I decided:**
- **Follow-up after deletion:** the deleted person can't follow their own delete operation, because their token stops working once it succeeds. They can watch `GET /accounts/me` turn to 403 instead.
- **Data left behind:**
  - *Tracker:* it still keeps the operations the account started; the storm leaves Tracker out.
  - *Other people's notifications:* those about notes the deleted account archived stay, because they belong to their recipients.
  - *`editedBy`:* versions the account made in someone else's note keep its id, which no longer names an account.
- **Timing:** the other contexts forget the account a moment after the delete succeeds. Nothing can be added in that window, because the token no longer authenticates.
- **Reminders on deleted notes:** they aren't cancelled through Notes. The notification they planned belonged to the deleted owner, and Notifications removes it anyway.
- **Hard delete:** the account is removed from the store outright, with no "deleted" marker left behind. That is what lets its email sign up again.

Search now works, committed as `bc38372` on the current branch (not pushed). The gate passes on every step, including the unit and end-to-end tests. The storm owes nothing and is marked `done: true`.

**How it's built.** As the storm decided, search reads what Notes already holds: no new context, relationship or ADR.
- **`GET /notes/search?q=`:** answers `[{ id, title, ownerId }]`, most recent first. It covers the caller's own notes and those shared with them, and leaves archived notes out.
- **Refusals:** a missing or blank `q` gets 400 (a new `BlankSearchQuery` refusal), and an anonymous caller gets 403.
- **Parsing the query:** a small `SearchQuery` value object splits it on whitespace, lower-cases it, drops duplicate words and refuses it when blank. The read side does the matching.
- **Tests:** specs cover the query parsing, the read side's filter and order, and the handler, plus an end-to-end case.

**What was unclear, and what I decided:**
- **Where the words can be:** each word may be in the title or in the text; they don't all have to be in the same one. So "rome train" finds a note titled "Train times" whose text says "Rome trip". The other reading — all words in the title, or all in the text — would be a one-line change in `InMemoryNoteQueries.search`.
- **Partial words match:** "contains" is a plain substring match, so `rom` finds "Rome". There is no whole-word or accent-insensitive matching.
- **Words are split on whitespace only:** punctuation stays part of a word.
- **Anonymous caller with a blank query:** gets 403, because who is calling is checked before the query.
- **Notes shared with an editor:** they are found like any other shared note; the editor role makes no difference to search.
